As the Resolution Plan could not be finalized within the prescribed timeline, the Committee of Creditors approved the initiation of liquidation proceedings. the Honble NCLAT vide its order dated March 16, 2021, passed the order for liquidation. Successful Applicant submitted the highest bid and was declared the successful bidder for acquisition of KS Oils Limited as a going concern. Thereafter Successful Applicant approached the NCLT for requisite directions and approvals for effecting transfer of the Corporate Debtor. The Honble NCLT, Indore Bench, passed an order in this matter on February 3, 2025. Pursuant to the aforesaid order, The new Board was reconstituted and the erstwhile Directors and KMP were deemed to have resigned/vacated office with effect from February 07, 2025. Thereafter the Company filed an application for relisting of its equity shares. The Exchanges thereafter issued a circular withdrawing the delisting, and the status of the equity shares changed from Delisted to Suspended. remarksWeb: 1) Indraprastha Medical Corporation Limited (the Company) is a joint venture between the Government of NCT of Delhi (GNCTD) and Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Limited (AHEL), both being the promoters of the Company.      At the time of incorporation of the Company in 1988, Ms. Vineeta Rai, then an officer of the GNCTD, was one of the subscribers to the Memorandum and Articles of Association (MOA & AOA). Accordingly, one equity share was allotted in her name as a subscriber under the Promoter category. The said share is beneficially owned by the GNCTD and continues to be held in physical form in her name.      The Company has repeatedly requested the GNCTD to transfer the said share from the names of its former officials to the name of the President of India. However, the transfer is yet to be effected.      Ms. Vineeta Rai retired from Government service long ago and was appointed as an Independent Director of the Company with effect from 8 February 2021.      2) Ms. Sangita Reddy (PAN AASPS6786K) is holding 8600 shares which were allotted under the Promoters category in the share capital of the Company. name: Bhagyanagar India Limited
shareholdingPatternNotes: NOTE An auto-disseminated disclosure has appeared on the BSE / NSE portal under the System Driven Disclosure (SDD) mechanism maintained by CDSL, indicating an off-market sale of 12,73,335 equity shares of Bhagyanagar India Limited by Mr. Devendra Surana on December 29, 2025. In this regard, it is clarified that Mr. Devendra Surana is a Promoter and Managing Director of Bhagyanagar India Limited. The Company has a wholly owned subsidiary, Bhagyanagar Copper Private Limited, which is engaged in the manufacturing of copper products and, as a standard commercial practice, undertakes hedging of copper prices in the derivatives market to mitigate price volatility. For undertaking such hedging activity, margin security was required to be provided by way of pledge of shares held by the promoter. Due to certain technical constraints, the pledge could not be created directly from the demat account of Mr. Devendra Surana. Accordingly, to facilitate the pledge for business purposes, Mr. Devendra Surana transferred 12,73,335 equity shares of Bhagyanagar India Limited to the demat account of Bhagyanagar Copper Private Limited through an off-market transaction, clearly marked as transfer between director and company (Reason Code 90). No consideration was paid or received in connection with the said transfer. Subsequent to receipt of the shares, Bhagyanagar Copper Private Limited immediately created the requisite pledge and completed the hedge transaction. The movement of shares was a one-time technical transaction undertaken solely to safeguard the business interests of the Group. Accordingly, since no consideration was involved and the transfer was effected purely for pledge creation, the transaction does not constitute a sale or purchase of shares and should not be construed as such under the provisions of SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, or SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.

Under the terms of the Promoter Agreement, the BSA Promoter Group has undertaken that they shall not, directly or indirectly transfer or encumber equity securities in the Company other than pursuant to (i) a Permitted Sale that complies with Clause 6 (Transfer of Equity Securities) of the Agreement, including the right of first offer in favour of the Purchasers; or (ii) an encumbrance of equity securities up to 5% in aggregate of the share capital (or such additional equity securities as mutually agreed with the Purchaser in writing) by way of an Eligible Pledge; or (iii) a Permitted Sale of up to 3% of the share capital held by the BSA Promoter Group. These do not create any third party interest in these shares. As the definition of Encumbrance in the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 is broadly worded, the disclosure has been made on June 09, 2025 out of abundant caution. As no pledge or lien has been created on 30 May 2025, the number of encumbered shares continues to remain the same as the details set out in Promoter holding already pledged and reported under column XIV of the Shareholding pattern.
